S9.01.needs: a paid account with Work available (not a Free trial) and at least two library files
S9.01.note: The Files menu is also reachable from the plus button, which offers "Add photos & files"; the search box only appears in the Files menu.
steps: Turn on Work mode from the composer mode choice labelled "Work".
Click "Files" in the work bar under the message box.
Type part of a file name in the box "Search library files".
Look: the list shows only files whose names match what you typed, compared with Expected.
S9.01.where: Chat composer > Work mode > "Files" in the work bar above the message box > "Search library files"

steps: Open a new chat.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Type a model name in "Search models" and click a different model.
Look: the model name on the button changes to the one you picked, compared with Expected.
S9.02.where: Chat composer, bottom row > the model name button (screen-reader name ends "Change model") > "Models" list > "Search models"

S9.03.needs: a paid account with Deep Research; a connected app for the Connected app option
S9.03.note: The source choice is part of the research run plan, not a picker on the first screen of a normal chat.
steps: Click the plus button and choose "Deep Research".
Send a research question so the "Research plan" panel opens.
In "Add a source" pick a kind: "Only this site", "Never this site", "My files" or "Connected app", type or choose a value, then click "Add".
Look: the chip list "Sources for this run" shows the added source, compared with Expected.
S9.03.where: Chat composer > plus button (screen-reader name "More composer options") > "Deep Research" > "Research plan" panel > "Add a source"

S9.04.needs: a connector with two linked accounts
S9.04.note: Searched for account pickers ("Choose account", "Select account", "accounts.map", "Connected account") under apps/web/features and packages/ui. Found only a read-only list of accounts, "Connected account" heading, in apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx, with no control to pick one.

S9.05.needs: a team workspace on the account
S9.05.note: The account button's screen-reader name is "Account menu for <name>" in apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx.
steps: Open the account menu from the sidebar.
Hover or click "Workspace".
Look at the list: "Personal" and any team workspaces.
Click a different workspace; a confirmation may appear, then check the active workspace changed, compared with Expected.
S9.05.where: Account menu for your name (sidebar) > "Workspace" > "Personal" or a team workspace name

S9.06.needs: a paid account with Work available and at least one project
steps: Turn on Work mode in the composer.
Click "Project" in the work bar under the message box.
Type a project name in "Search projects...".
Click a project and look: the button shows that project name, compared with Expected.
S9.06.where: Chat composer > "Project" in the work bar (reads "Project or folder" in Work mode) > "Search projects..."

S9.07.needs: a connected GitHub account with repositories, or a public repository URL
steps: Open Code from the sidebar.
Click the "Select repository" chip.
Type in "Search repositories" to narrow the list, or type a URL such as the placeholder "https://github.com/owner/repository".
Click a repository and look: the chip shows its name, compared with Expected.
S9.07.where: Code (sidebar) > composer > "Select repository" chip > "Search repositories" or the URL box

labels.text: Search or type a branch name

S9.08.needs: a repository with more than one branch
steps: Choose a repository in Code.
Click the branch chip.
Look at the "Branches" list, then type in "Search or type a branch name" to filter.
Click another branch and look: the chip shows that branch, compared with Expected.
S9.08.where: Code (sidebar) > choose a repository > branch chip (screen-reader name "Change the branch") > "Search or type a branch name"

S9.09.needs: a microphone and a second audio output device to see a real choice
S9.09.note: Only an audio output picker was found. No microphone or camera picker was found in AudioRoutePicker.tsx or VoiceComposer.tsx.
steps: Click "Start voice mode" in the composer.
Click the "Audio output" button.
Look at the list "Audio output device" with "System default" and any other speakers.
Pick a device and look: the button shows that device, compared with Expected.
S9.09.where: Chat > "Start voice mode" > "Audio output" button in the voice screen

S9.10.needs: a signed-in account; creating a key is only needed to see the result
S9.10.note: Once-versus-always choices are on the approval card: "Allow", "Allow for this chat" and "Deny" in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts. Site automation scope was not found.
steps: Open Settings > Account and click the "API keys" row.
Click "Generate Key".
Look at the scope list: "Read model catalog", "Run inference", "Read usage", and tick only some of them.
Create the key and look at the key list: it shows only the scopes you ticked, compared with Expected.
S9.10.where: Settings > Account > "API keys" > "Generate Key" (scope checkboxes); also chat composer > "Tool approvals" in Work mode

S9.11.needs: a second account in the same workspace
S9.11.note: No search-by-name or email input was found. Only a list of existing members with per-person access choices, so the picker part of Expected is not present.
steps: Open Projects and open one of your projects.
Open the more-options menu and click "Share".
Look at the dialog: the list "People with access to <project>", each person with a Read, Write or None choice, and the sharing select "Everyone in the workspace can view" or "Only people you invite".
Change one person's access and look: the choice is saved and shown, compared with Expected.
S9.11.where: Projects (sidebar) > open a project > the more-options menu > "Share" > "Share <project name>" dialog

steps: Open Scheduled and click "New task".
Fill "Schedule Name" and "Task Instructions".
Open "Frequency" and choose "One Time", "Daily", "Weekly", "Monthly", "Interval", "Custom Cron" or "Recurrence Rule"; the fields below change to match.
Save and look at the schedule row: its cadence matches what you chose, compared with Expected.

S9.13.needs: a few uploaded or generated files
steps: Open Library.
Look at the tabs: "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Artifacts", "Uploads", "Generated files".
Type a name in "Search the library by name".
Click a file and look: it opens in the file viewer ("Close file viewer"), compared with Expected.

S9.14.needs: a skill with folders in its files
steps: Open Settings and click "Skills".
Open a skill that has folders.
In the "Skill files" tree, click a folder row to expand it, then click again to collapse it.
Look: the folder opens and closes and the file inside is reached, compared with Expected.
S9.14.where: Settings > Skills (under the Customize group) > open a skill > "Skill files" tree

S9.15.note: The sort is reached through a title on the heading, so a tester may need to hover to see it.
steps: Ask for a spreadsheet in a chat and open the artifact.
Open the artifacts panel if it is closed.
Click a column heading; its title reads "Sort by <column>". Click again to reverse, then clear.
Look: the rows reorder by that column, compared with Expected.
S9.15.where: Chat > open a spreadsheet artifact ("Open artifacts panel") > click a column heading

steps: Open Library.
Click the "Grid view" button in the "Library layout" group.
Look: files and artifacts appear as cards with a preview.
Click "List view" to switch back, compared with Expected.
S9.16.where: Library (sidebar) > "Grid view" button in the toolbar

S9.17.needs: at least one image in the library
steps: Open Library and click the "Images" tab.
Look at the picture tiles in the grid.
Click one picture to open it in the larger viewer.
Look at the enlarged picture, then click "Close file viewer", compared with Expected.

S9.19.needs: a paid account with Work available
steps: Turn on Work mode and send a task that uses tools.
Look at the "Agent activity" section while it runs.
Check the steps are listed in order, each with its state and a running seconds counter where shown.
Compare with Expected once the run finishes.
S9.19.where: Chat in Work mode > run a task > "Agent activity" section

steps: Open Settings and click "Account".
Scroll to the bottom to the "Recent activity" panel.
Make a small change elsewhere in settings, then come back.
Look: the newest event is at the top, compared with Expected.

S9.21.needs: a few work runs in different states
S9.21.note: The sidebar label "Work" comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json; the sidebar entry itself was not traced.
steps: Open Work from the sidebar to reach "Work history" (or go to /tasks).
Click "Board" in the "Task layout" control.
Look: columns with headings "Queued", "Running", "Needs approval", "Done" (and others with runs) and a count per column.
Click "List" to switch back, compared with Expected.

S9.22.note: No "Back" control was found in GalleryClient.tsx, so going back is not visible; Expected says it should be.
steps: Open /gallery and click "Create artifact".
Look at the step counter text "Step <n> of <total>" and the step dots.
Click "Next" to move forward; the counter and dots advance.
Look: the counter matches the step shown, compared with Expected.
S9.22.where: Gallery page (/gallery) > "Create artifact" > pick a type > "Next" steps

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S9.23.note: The wizard has two steps (name, first task). No model or sign-in choice step was found in OnboardingWizard.tsx.
steps: Create a new account and reach the welcome page.
Look for "Step 1 of 2" and the "Preferred name" field.
Type a name and continue; check "Step 2 of 2" with "What do you want to do first?".
Finish and check the name appears, compared with Expected.
S9.23.where: New account sign-up > welcome page (/welcome) > "What should we call you?"

S9.24.needs: a desktop-width window and an artifact
steps: Open a chat that has an artifact and click "Open artifacts panel".
Drag the separator named "Resize artifacts panel" left or right.
Or click the separator and press the Left or Right arrow key.
Look: the artifact pane gets wider or narrower and the chat pane adjusts, compared with Expected.
S9.24.where: Chat > "Open artifacts panel" > separator "Resize artifacts panel" between chat and artifact

S9.26.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
steps: Open an artifact that has been edited more than once.
Click the version counter (screen-reader name "Version <n> of <total>. Show version history").
Look at the "Version history" panel: each saved version and its count.
Click "Restore version <n>" on an older one and look: the artifact shows that version, compared with Expected.
S9.26.where: Chat > open an artifact > version counter "Version <n> of <total>" > "Version history"

S9.27.needs: a coding session with uncommitted or committed changes
steps: Open a coding session that has changed files.
Click "Changes" in the header; the panel opens.
Use "Filter changed files" if needed and click a file to read its diff.
Look: added and removed lines are marked, compared with Expected. Do not click "Discard" controls.
S9.27.where: Code > a coding session with file changes > "Changes" in the header

S9.28.needs: a web-search answer (a question that triggers web sources)
S9.28.note: Whether a web-search answer is produced depends on the model and the question; the Sources button only appears when the answer has sources.
steps: Sign in and ask a question that needs web search, such as a current news topic.
Wait until the answer finishes, then click the Sources button under the answer.
In the research panel, read the Sources tab: each row shows the title, the publisher and date line (with Retrieved date) and a short snippet.
Click a source row; it opens the page in a new tab. Compare with Expected: title, origin, excerpt, and open.
S9.28.where: Chat > send a question that uses web search > under the answer, click Sources > click a source row

S9.29.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees Upgrade for higher capacity instead)
S9.29.note: The meter is labelled for assistive tech with '<name> usage' and the percent as its value; screen-reader output was not checked.
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings, then click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look at each bar: Current session, This week and, when shown, Most capable models. Each shows a percent used.
Read the reset line under a bar (Resets at ... or a time left until reset) and compare with Expected: percent, window and reset time.
S9.29.where: Account menu > Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits

S9.30.needs: a paid account (the card is hidden on Free plans and on contract-priced accounts)
S9.30.note: The card only appears once the usage data has loaded; the Buy credits button uses the billing settings section.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits with their amounts.
Click Buy credits and see that it opens the Billing section. Compare with Expected: balance and an add-credits button in one place.
S9.30.where: Account menu > Settings > Usage > Credit balances

S9.31.needs: a connector that uses OAuth permissions; an outside account (for example Google) to finish connecting
S9.31.note: Connectors with no OAuth scopes show a note instead: This provider does not use OAuth scopes.
steps: Open Settings, then click Connectors.
Click a connector that asks for sign-in permissions.
Find the Permissions requested box and read each permission sentence with its Read or Write badge.
Click Connect; the dialog Connect <name>? repeats the list with Deny and Allow buttons. Compare with Expected: what the connector may do and whether it is read or write.
S9.31.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector that uses sign-in > Permissions requested

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S9.32.needs: a tool that asks for approval (the policy setting above must be on); a paid account may be needed for some tools
S9.32.note: Which tools trigger an approval card was not confirmed from the code; Allow for this chat is hidden for high-risk tools.
steps: Open Settings, click Capabilities, find the Tool approvals box and choose Ask before every action.
Go to a chat and send a request that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a connected app or site action).
When the action pauses, read the inline line that says the tool requires approval, and the buttons Allow, Allow for this chat and Deny.
Click Deny and check that the run stops; repeat and click Allow and check that the run continues. Compare with Expected.
S9.32.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > Ask before every action, then in chat send a request that uses a tool

S9.33.needs: an outside account for the connector (for example Google)
S9.33.note: No Expired word exists in the code; a connection that needs signing in again shows the notice '<name> needs reconnecting' and a Reconnect button (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts).
steps: Open Settings, click Connectors, then click a connector that is not connected.
Read the notice You're not connected to <name> yet. and the Connect button.
Click Connect and finish the sign-in; the button should change to Connected.
Open the remove control for a connected card (Disconnect) and check that the state returns to not connected. Compare with Expected.

labels.text: cannot read images, so the images in this conversation will be ignored.
Older messages will be left out of the next reply.

S9.34.needs: a file to upload (an image); a model that cannot read images in your list
S9.34.note: Which models lack image or tool support depends on the live model catalogue, so the tester must pick one from the list; the notice is a visible line, its aria label Model compatibility is not visible.
steps: In a chat, choose a model from the model picker below the message box.
Attach an image file to the message, without sending.
Read the notice above the message box that says the chosen model cannot read images.
Change to a model that reads images and check the notice disappears. Compare with Expected: warning shown before sending.
S9.34.where: Chat > choose a model that cannot read images (model picker under the message box) > attach an image > read the notice above the message box

S9.35.needs: a task that runs several steps (agent or work mode)
S9.35.note: The count only shows when the task has steps; which tasks produce steps depends on the model and request.
steps: Send a request that makes the assistant run a multi-step task.
While it runs, click the Progress panel at the bottom of the chat.
Read the count (for example 1/4) and the current action line; wait and see them change.
When the task ends, check the final state and the count. Compare with Expected: state, progress and latest action updating.
S9.35.where: Chat > start a task that runs several steps > open the Progress panel at the bottom of the chat

S9.36.note: Showing the card depends on the assistant deciding to ask; other interactive cards (map, answer cards) also render in InteractiveCardBlock.tsx and were not separately tested.
steps: Ask a vague request that needs a choice, such as planning a trip without a destination.
When a card with options appears in the answer, click one or more options.
Click Send answers and check that the card shows Sending, then that the answer continues using your choice.
S9.36.where: Chat > ask a question the assistant needs to clarify > pick options on the card > Send answers

S9.37.needs: at least one notification (for example a finished scheduled run)
S9.37.note: Unread state is also announced to screen readers with the hidden text ', unread'; the screen-reader output itself was not checked.
steps: Click the bell icon in the sidebar next to the app name.
Read the Notifications list: newest first, unread items in bold with a dot.
Click one unread item; it opens its page and is marked read.
Click Mark all as read and check that the unread marks go away. Compare with Expected.
S9.37.where: Sidebar > the bell icon next to the app name > Notifications

S9.38.note: The Return key behaviour was not confirmed in the file; the shortcut is handled as metaKey or ctrlKey plus k in CommandPaletteProvider.tsx.
steps: Press Command+K on the Mac keyboard.
Type part of a command or chat name, such as Settings.
Check that the list narrows as you type.
Use the arrow keys and press Return on Go to Settings and check that the app opens Settings.
S9.38.where: Any signed-in screen > press Command+K (Ctrl+K on Windows or Linux) > type in the box Search chats and actions > press Return
